findings.message: The header of the criteria file has no "weight" column, so it cannot give the weights; they are read from the scores file.
findings.subject: weight
findings.fix: Add the column named to the spreadsheet; docs/inputs.md lists every column. The evidence and red_flag columns may be left out, and then every evidence and every red flag is read as empty.
findings.own: Asking for these columns is a best practice of this tool; no standard sets it; the names are the tool's own, because no standard fixes the columns of a scorecard

findings.message: The required cell of row 5 of the criteria file, "maybe", is not yes or no; the criterion is read as not required.
findings.subject: References
findings.fix: Write yes or no, or leave the cell empty.
findings.own: Reading only yes and no is a best practice of this tool; no standard sets it; a red flag written as "maybe" or "y" would otherwise pass as no flag

findings.message: The criterion "Token design" is in the criteria file, but was scored by no vendor: no row of the scores file scores it. It counts for nothing in the weighted scores.
findings.subject: Token design
findings.fix: Score the criterion for the vendors, or take it out of the criteria file and the scores file.
findings.own: Listing a criterion nobody scored is a best practice of this tool; no standard sets it; it takes weight in the sheet and counts for nothing in the ranking, which looks like a decision and is not one

findings.message: The column "Note" has the same name as column 7 of the scores file once case and separators are ignored; only the first is read.

findings.own: Refusing a column written twice is a best practice of this tool; no standard sets it; two readers could see two values

findings.message: A cell of the column "note" is shaped like a mnemonic. The tool never reads a seed or a key, and the value is not shown.
